title: After 6 weeks off, the Profile's 'kg to lift' goal still asks for at least the old total, while each exercise card plans a lighter start
what: When a member comes back after a break of 6 weeks or more, each exercise card plans a lighter start (10 to 30 percent less) and says 'Back after 8 weeks, so a lighter start'. The Profile's Next line adds the exercises up differently: for each one it takes the larger of the planned sets and the previous sets, so its 'kg to lift' number is the old total and reads 'Same as previous'. The same happens when the plan has fewer sets than last time: the cards say the target is not above previous, the Next line still shows the previous total as the goal. The big number is then higher than the cards add up to, and gives no reason.
expected: The Next line's goal is the sum of what the exercise cards plan, and after a long break or a shorter plan it says why the goal is lower than previous, the same way the cards do.
how_often: every member back after 6 weeks or more, until the first workout back
fix_line: Add up the planned sets as the cards plan them (no lift to the previous total on a long break or a shorter plan) and say the reason on the Next line

title: 'Kg lifted' on a share picture is a different number from 'Kg lifted' in the app for the same workout or month
what: For pull-ups, dips and other body-weight moves, the finish screen and the monthly report count part of the member's body weight in 'Kg lifted'. The share pictures of that workout and that month leave body weight out on purpose, to keep it private, but keep the same label 'KG LIFTED'. A member who trains pull-ups sees, say, 3,104 kg lifted in the app and a much smaller KG LIFTED (or REPS) on the picture of the same workout or month, with nothing saying why.
expected: The same label shows the same number everywhere, or the picture's number has its own name (for example 'Kg on the bar') so a member is not left wondering which is right.
how_often: every share picture of a workout or month with body-weight moves
fix_line: Give the picture's number its own label, or add a short line under it saying body weight is left out

items.reason: This area holds no gym facts (alerts, dues, plan end, birthdays, members using the app); its member facts were listed by place: kg lifted (finish screen, workout picture, month report page, month picture, Profile Next line, exercise card), workouts this week (Up next card, calendar), days trained (month report, month picture). Workouts live only on the phone, so a Crispy Curves data count cannot show them; compared in code.
Rule applied: picture kg lifted vs app kg lifted differs (new 02); weekly goal counts days not workouts (existing); picture 'more than previous' counts body weight (existing).

Date edges read: long break (6+ weeks) target vs Next line, first time on a routine, no previous kilos, month bar ranges (whole month, single day), calendar months back to the first workout, photo 'weeks apart', report 'so far' rows. Only the long-break goal is wrong.
Rule applied: the Profile goal is wrong after a long break.

Summaries vs their rows: calendar month and year totals add the same per-day counts the grid shows; share picture set count is the sum of the rows' working sets; finish screen 'Mostly X' picks from the same rows; exercise card total is the sum of its set rows; the Profile goal is NOT the sum of the card plans.
Rule applied: the goal differs from its rows with no reason; card drops (break, fewer sets, step back) all carry a reason line.
Opened the files that work numbers out: the goal, card target, finish compare, calendar, months, chart ranges, report rows and share picture numbers, plus the engine break rule.

Profile goal number: todayGoalFrom; its rows (exercise cards): kgPlan. Finish total vs rows: one delta list feeds both. Calendar total: monthTotal over the same per-day map. Picture sets: same working-set rule for total and rows.
Goal and card are two functions; on a long-gap case (6+ weeks, 10-30 percent lighter plan) the goal keeps the old total while the cards plan less.
